messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: router-service p99 latency crossed 2.5s in us-west2; streaming stalls observed on long-lived connections. Pager sent to @sre_oncall_maria and @alex_router — please ack and triage. https://dash.redwood-internal.com/d/routers/latency?orgId=1&from=now-30m

sre_oncall_maria: acked, I'm on it. digging into p95/p99 and streaming sessions now. oncall bridge if we need it.

alex_router: I'm up. seeing a sharp spike at ~1799501200, tail dominated by a few shards. p95 ~800ms -> 1.2s, p99 -> 2.6s. streaming stalls correlate with increased request fanout and queue depth on router-node-7*.

jamal_platform: FYI we pushed a loadbalancer policy rollout (policy id roll-2026-03-15-42) ~30m ago to prefer local affinity. Could be weight skew. reverting is an option if this aligns.

sre_oncall_maria: grabbing heap/conn metrics. @alex_router can you dump the routing heatmap and top keys?

alex_router: paste dump of top hotkeys and per-shard qdepth below:
```
TOP HOT KEYS (last 15m):
- tenant:payments:acct-9832 -> 18% of requests
- tenant:chat:room-4b9 -> 12% of requests
SHARD QUEUE DEPTH (sample):
- router-node-7a: qdepth 128
- router-node-7b: qdepth 142
- router-node-2c: qdepth 12
```

liz_support: getting customer reports — two streaming customers reported stalls and reconnects starting ~12:30pm PT, both on us-west2 region. CS has ticket numbers: CS-44912, CS-44915. They flagged increased error rates and timeouts.

ops-bot: Incident bridge created: https://meet.redwood/bridge/1799502468 (auto). Pager escalation to SRE pager + eng-router.

jamal_platform: looked at rollout diff: we bumped prefer_local weight from 0.6 -> 0.85 in us-west2 to reduce cross-zone egress. That will concentrate traffic on local nodes and can accidentally create hot partitions if hotkeys are present.

sre_oncall_maria: that matches. we have a small set of hot keys (payments acct) getting pushed to same local shard due to affinity bump. That explains tail. immediate mitigation options: 1) roll back policy, 2) manually rebalance weights for hotkey paths, 3) add short-term key hashing tweak. Rollback is fastest.

alex_router: rolling back is lower risk. prepare rollback plan. I can trigger rollback via control-plane API.

jamal_platform: agree. Also watching streaming stalls: long-lived connections still show stalls even after qdepth drops because some nodes are saturated CPU-wise with kv-cache misses. Might need to shift streaming traffic away from the hot nodes rather than kill connections.

sre_oncall_maria: initiating rollback now — calling control plane: 
```
# rollback prefer_local rollout
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/rollouts/roll-2026-03-15-42/rollback \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"reason":"emergency rollback - tail latency spike"}'
```

incident-bot: rollback job accepted: job-id rb-1799502499. Estimated completion 30s.

ops-bot: Deploybot: rollback applied to 80% of edges, finishing.

alex_router: telemetry update: p99 dropping from 2.6s -> 1.4s in next 2m. p95 also trending down. streaming stall rate still ~40% of previous baseline for long sessions.

liz_support: customers still seeing reconnects but fewer errors. CS oncall will keep tickets open and notify customers of mitigation.

jamal_platform: I think remaining streaming issues are caused by hot partition on node group router-node-7*, which sustained higher CPU and KV cache churn. We should drain the hot shard and fail traffic to spare nodes. Draining plan: mark shard as draining and shift routes with weight 0.0 for 10m, then resume gradual traffic.

sre_oncall_maria: agree. steps: 1) mark node as maintenance (control plane) 2) shift 100% of ingress for affected prefixes to fallback pool 3) monitor tail and streaming stalls 4) uncordon when healthy. I'll run commands.

alex_router: command snippets below — using the admin api:
```
# mark node group draining
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/nodes/router-node-7/drain -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN"
# set routing weight to fallback pool
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/routing/weights -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" -d '{"prefix":"tenant:payments:", "weights": {"fallback-pool": 1.0}}'
```

incident-bot: Maintenance flag applied to router-node-7 group. Traffic shift started.

jamal_platform: seeing immediate qdepth improvements on 7a/7b, CPU falling ~60% -> ~30% on those nodes. Streaming stall rate dropping but not fully recovered.

sre_oncall_maria: metrics now: p95 420ms, p99 680ms, streaming stall rate ~12% above baseline (was +300% at peak). Good progress.

alex_router: starting controlled slow-drain would be safer than abrupt disconnects for long-lived streaming. Using graceful conn handoff TTL=45s.

liz_support: CS updated customers with interim mitigation and ETA for full recovery. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident severity reduced to SEV-2. Pager de-escalation scheduled in 30m if metrics remain stable.

jamal_platform: quick note — the rollout logic did not account for skewed key distributions when prefer_local weight > 0.8; we'll add a safety guard to cap affinity weight for prefixes with >5% traffic. Filed follow-up: ENG-1799.

sre_oncall_maria: agreed, file a postmortem and assign owners. Primary actions for P0->P1: rollback, drain hot group, apply temporary fallback weights. Follow-ups: add rollout guard, improve heatmap alerting for hotkey concentration.

alex_router: creating a short ticket for runtime fix + tests: RT-4287 (affinity-cap + unit).

liz_support: I'm drafting a customer note for affected accounts and will attach timeline once we stabilize.

incident-bot: Metrics back to within SLO window for p99 in us-west2. Monitoring for 20m before closing timeline.

sre_oncall_maria: final checks: no customer-facing errors reported for 10m, p99 holding ~550-700ms. I'll remain on the bridge for another 15m then hand off to follow-up doc owners.

alex_router: handing off to @jamal_platform for postmortem writeup and to @liz_support for customer comms. thanks all. :sparkles:

jamal_platform: will draft postmortem and include mitigation scripts. assigning owners: jamal -> root cause + fix, alex -> runtime tests, maria -> alerting improvements, liz -> customer comms.

sre_oncall_maria: closing incident channel in 25m if stable. Good job team. :clap:

ops-bot: Incident closed draft generated. Follow-up checklist: rollback verification, confirm rb-1799502499 details, ENG-1799 created, RT-4287 created, CS tickets updated.

liz_support: adding customer note drafts to CS tickets.

jamal_platform: quick note for postmortem: timeline, metrics, rollback job id, node drain commands, and the change that caused it (roll-2026-03-15-42). I'll attach logs and the heatmap snapshot.

sre_oncall_maria: thanks — linking the incident runbook and will schedule a small retro with eng-router tomorrow.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Close if stable for 20m.
